goldenBlueMethod: Golden/blue hour windows are computed, not independently sourced: blue hour = the civil-twilight window either side of sunrise/sunset (sun -6 deg to 0 deg elevation, taken directly from the sunrise-sunset.org civil-twilight fields above); golden hour = standard photography convention (sun approx -4 deg to +6 deg elevation), approximated here as roughly 50 minutes bracketing sunrise/sunset for this latitude (26.5N) in early September. Two dedicated golden-hour calculators (golden-hour.com, sunrisesunsetcalendar.com) were unreachable (TLS cert mismatch / DNS failure), so these minute-level boundaries are a derived estimate, not a third-party figure - treat +/-10min as the real precision.
tempNote: Typical early-September diurnal curve for Ajmer, built from the Ajmer climate-normal table (Sept mean daily max 33.6C, mean daily min 24.3C) and shaped against actual Sept 1-5 2026 daily observations (highs 26-33C) from Weather Underground. Not an hour-by-hour measured curve for 6 Sept 2026 specifically - no hourly historical/forecast source was reachable (Wunderground, AccuWeather and climate-data.org hourly pages all returned 403/404).
humidity: 60-90% range across early Sept 2026 (Weather Underground daily obs for Ajmer, Sept 1-5): typically highest just after sunrise and after rain, lowest mid-afternoon (~55-65%) between rain spells.
monsoon: Active / recently active over the region as of 6 Sept 2026. IMD bulletins (mausam.imd.gov.in) reported isolated heavy-to-very-heavy rainfall over East Rajasthan and West Madhya Pradesh on 3-5 Sept 2026 from a low-pressure system, with a further note of subdued rainfall over Peninsular India (not Rajasthan specifically) for the following week. Ajmer's own actual readings on 4-5 Sept 2026 were cooler and far more humid (26-30C, humidity up to 90%) than 1-3 Sept (32-33C, 60-67%), consistent with that rain system reaching Ajmer district. No IMD announcement of monsoon withdrawal from Rajasthan was found as of this check; normal LPA withdrawal onset for west Rajasthan is mid-to-late September, so the monsoon should be treated as still technically active over Ajmer on 6 Sept 2026, just past a wet spell.
rainChance: Not independently confirmed for 6 Sept 2026 itself (no dated IMD nowcast for that specific day was found). Given a rain system passed through 3-5 Sept and IMD flagged only 'subdued' activity for Peninsular India (a different region) afterward, treat as: skies likely humid/partly cloudy with a residual, not-zero, chance of an afternoon shower - this line is a reasoned inference from the surrounding bulletins, not a sourced number, and is listed in unverified below.
heatWindowNote: Peak of the 31-33C midday/afternoon plateau, compounded by monsoon-season humidity (heat-index effect, not just dry heat). Locals and shopkeepers in both towns commonly take an afternoon lull in this window - many small shops and stalls slow down or shut 13:00-16:00, ghat/temple footfall thins, and open-air sightseeing (Pushkar lake parikrama, Ajmer fort walks) is pushed to before 11:00 or after 17:00.
moon: Waning crescent, approx 28% illuminated (moon age ~24 days into the synodic month), per moongiant.com for 6 Sept 2026. Not near Purnima or Amavasya: 6 Sept 2026 falls roughly 10 days after the last full moon (~27-28 Aug 2026) and roughly 5 days before the next new moon (~11 Sept 2026), both dates derived, not independently sourced.
tithi: Krishna Paksha Dashami (10th day of the waning fortnight), Bhadrapada month, Vikram Samvat 2083, ending approx 19:29 IST on 6 Sept 2026 (then moving into Ekadashi). Panchang figures were pulled from Delhi/Ahmedabad-calibrated pages, not an Ajmer-specific panchang - the tithi/day itself will not change for Ajmer's slightly different longitude, but the exact hour the tithi ends could shift by a few minutes; treat only the hour-level figure as approximate.
lunarSignificance: Nothing special for Pushkar Lake specifically on 6 Sept 2026 - it is an ordinary Krishna Paksha Dashima, not a Purnima or Amavasya. Pushkar's major lunar-linked pilgrimage dates (the big lake-bathing mela) fall on Kartik Purnima in Oct/Nov, not Bhadrapada - no lake-specific crowd effect expected from the lunar calendar this week.

festivals.name: Krishna Janmashtami
festivals.effect: 2 days before 6 Sept. Temple crowds/decorations in Ajmer and Pushkar temples would have peaked on the 4th; some residual festive decoration but not active crowding by the 6th.

festivals.name: Dahi Handi
festivals.effect: 1 day before 6 Sept, linked to Janmashtami. Localised street events, not a Pushkar/Ajmer pilgrimage draw.

festivals.name: Aja Ekadashi
festivals.effect: 1 day after 6 Sept. A monthly fasting/pilgrimage day observed by many Vaishnavite pilgrims - can bring a modest uptick in ritual bathers at Pushkar ghats on the 7th itself, not the 6th. This is a routine monthly Ekadashi, not a mega-event on the scale of Kartik Purnima.

festivals.name: Ganesh Chaturthi / Hartalika Teej
festivals.effect: 8 days after 6 Sept - outside the 'few days' window, listed only so it is not missed by a traveller extending their stay. No effect on 6 Sept itself.

festivalOn6Sept: No Hindu or regional festival falls on 6 September 2026 itself in Ajmer or Pushkar. It sits in the quiet gap between Janmashtami/Dahi Handi (4-5 Sept) and Aja Ekadashi (7 Sept).
aqi: Typically 'moderate', roughly 70 US AQI / ~19-32 ug/m3 PM2.5 per IQAir - September is one of the cleanest months of the year in Ajmer (post-monsoon rain washes out particulates), a sharp contrast to winter (Oct-Dec) when PM2.5 climbs well above 50 ug/m3. The 70 AQI figure was IQAir's live reading at the time of this check, not a verified value specifically for 6 Sept 2026.
